ink.role: type, rules, lit segments, inverted fills

unlit.role: a cell that is off; never text

rules: Red is the only hue and it always means 'off target'.
Red never carries meaning alone; a word or a density change says it too.
Intermediate tone is dot density (.nd-screen), never grey fill and never opacity.

faces.name: Dot matrix
faces.why: Ndot and NType82 are proprietary and cannot ship

faces.name: Space Grotesk
faces.why: Drawn from a monospace skeleton, so its squared letterforms share a family of shapes with the dot panel. Chosen against Ndot, NType82 and Lettera Mono LL on the running screens; those three are unlicensable or unbought.

typographyMeta.rootSize: 106.25% (17px default), a percentage so it multiplies the reader's own base size
typographyMeta.i18n: every visible string comes from next-intl; react/jsx-no-literals noStrings is enforced on src/**/*.tsx

shadows.note: No shadow, blur, gradient, translucency or layered surface anywhere. Separation is rules, inversion, or dot density.

motion.policy: one authored animation in the app

animations.name: nd-seek
animations.trigger: a macro strip whose target is not yet met
animations.reducedMotion: animation removed; all transitions clamped to 1ms

breakpoints.note: The desktop view is the phone view with air around it. No sidebar, no second column, no panel reflow.

components.name: Action
components.description: The only button: an inverted block, and the only filled element on a screen besides lit segments.

components.name: Rule
components.description: A 2px ink line. The world here is ruled sheets, not floating boxes.

components.name: Segment
components.description: The atom of the system. State is a string — off, on, over, short — never a boolean.

components.name: GlyphBar
components.description: Label and mono reading on one baseline, a full-width strip of segments, a status line. The strip is aria-hidden; the status line says the same fact in words.

components.name: MealLamps
components.description: One fixed-width lamp per meal, lit if the meal has food in it. Fixed-width because a stretched strip would read as a proportion.

components.name: DotText
components.description: The dot panel. Dots are aria-hidden and the real string sits in an sr-only span, so the panel renders the text rather than duplicating it.

components.name: TabSlot
components.description: Pictogram over label over a lamp. The active slot inverts and lights its lamp; inactive slots keep the lamp's space so nothing shifts.

narrative.overview: DietKit reports the state of one person's body and one day's plan. An instrument shows quantity as light: lamps that are on or off, digits built from dots, a rule where a card would be. The visual world is Nothing OS, pinned by the user and followed literally — the dot face is really built on a 5x7 cell, and the tab pictograms are drawn on that same grid. Reading order is the loop the product is: target, then how far the plan has got with it, then the body that says whether any of it is working.
keyCharacteristics: Two values and one red; every intermediate tone is dot density.
Quantity is rendered as light, never as a filled progress container.
Zero radius, zero shadow, zero gradient. Rules and inversion do all separation.
State is carried at least twice — by light and by words.
One authored motion in the whole app, stilled under prefers-reduced-motion.
One column at every width; the desktop view is the phone view with air around it.
rules: Red means something is off target, and never carries that alone.
--nd-dim is the entire secondary-ink budget; below it, remove the text.
A shaded surface is .nd-screen dots, never a grey fill and never opacity.
Pass .nd-seg a state name, never a boolean — a boolean renders unlit.
Every visible string lives in messages/pt-BR.json.
dos: Carry state by light and by words.
Reach for a rule before a container.
Give a quantity a readout: lamps if countable, a dot panel if it is the answer.
Size a dot panel from one fontSize; everything inside is in em.
donts: No faded type as a hierarchy device.
No radius, shadow or gradient, including the subtle kind.
No rendering the same number in two different voices.
No stretching a small-count indicator to full width.
narrative.notCanonized: The uppercase letter-spaced labels above headings read as eyebrows, which the craft floor bans. They are kept as a carried exception because a legend over a readout is native to the pinned instrument world — not promoted to house style, and still wrong in any other visual world in this codebase. Separately, /dieta, /peso, /alimentos, /perfil and /energia still carry the previous amber/emerald convention and are not described by this document.
